persons.name: Cakrarāja
persons.evidence: śrīcakrarājyasya ... sudhīś ca cakrarāja eva lekhayāñcakāraha

date.as_written: saṃvat 806 mārgaśira śudi 14 āditya(!)ra / ṣaḍabhravāruṇair yute śake caturddaśītithau pracaṇḍabhānuvāsare sumārgaśīrṣamāsi vai śuklapakṣamiśrite

notes: The catalogue lists Cakrarāja as scribe, but the text explicitly uses the causative 'lekhayāñcakāra' ('caused to be copied') and the genitive 'śrīcakrarājyasya' (for śrīcakrarājasya), identifying him as commissioner/patron. The date is given twice: first in Nepal Samvat prose (saṃvat 806 mārgaśira śudi 14 ādityavāra) and secondly in a Sanskrit verse referring to the Śaka era (śake).
